nodes.label: Default Configuration Isolation
nodes.rationale: Isolation is the default because inherited configuration increases prompt cost and re-enables sandbox drift.

nodes.label: Compact Filter
nodes.rationale: Compact is the default because the full agent message remains while often-redundant command output is replaced by its byte size.

nodes.label: Shared Tree Default
nodes.rationale: Shared-tree execution avoids manual collection and missing ignored dependencies; worktrees remain opt-in when writers overlap.

nodes.label: Explicit Cleanup Policy
nodes.rationale: Runs and worktrees are not cleaned automatically because they may hold the only durable handle or copy of produced work.

nodes.label: Managed Codex Subagent Harness
nodes.rationale: The repository is itself the harness: a Claude Code plugin that manages Codex CLI runs with safety, lifecycle, and context discipline.

nodes.label: Graphify-First Codebase Navigation
nodes.rationale: When graph data exists, scoped query/path/explain operations precede broad source browsing, and code changes are followed by an incremental graph update.

nodes.label: Native Delegation Invariants
nodes.rationale: Native parity is graded by outcome, safety, lifecycle burden, and recovery rather than by copying the surface shape of Agent or Workflow.

nodes.label: Filtered Event Context Discipline
nodes.rationale: Command aggregated output can contain whole files, so compact logs omit it and show retrieves one selected item explicitly.

nodes.label: Sandbox Reassertion Across Resume
nodes.rationale: Every resumed invocation must re-assert recorded settings because Codex resume re-derives them from the current config layer and can silently escalate or downgrade the sandbox.

nodes.label: Four Native-Parity Invariants
nodes.rationale: Parity is evaluated by achieved outcome, held safety invariants, absence of extra lifecycle steps, and recovery from error.

nodes.label: Config Defaults Preservation
nodes.rationale: Isolation should preserve only the user's model, reasoning effort, and service tier defaults, while sandbox remains owned by the harness invariant.

nodes.label: Shared Tree Batch Default
nodes.rationale: Measured native-subagent workflows showed automatic worktrees added collection steps and suppressed useful fan-out, so isolation became explicit with --worktree.

nodes.label: Finite Verification Predicate
nodes.rationale: A reviewer-generated finding count has no floor; verification should instead count a bounded artifact property such as reachable findings or a finite enumeration.

nodes.label: Adversarial Audit Method
nodes.rationale: Findings were independently challenged and only retained when concrete evidence or reproduction survived rebuttal.

nodes.label: Preserve Correct Mechanisms
nodes.rationale: Process-group stopping, context caps, doctor semantics, and the validated trigger boundary are explicitly protected from speculative cleanup.

nodes.label: Adaptive Phase Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Claude decides phase boundaries from prior results instead of freezing orchestration in a declarative plan file.

nodes.label: Capability Without Cost Policy
nodes.rationale: The bridge reports cost and exposes controls but does not impose concurrency or cleanup policy on the user.

nodes.label: Interface Owns Tool Facts
nodes.rationale: Facts the CLI can state belong in help, output, or refusals; prose keeps host facts and cross-command judgment so each claim has one owner.

nodes.label: Zero References Target
nodes.rationale: A reference file is justified only by a genuine reading branch with at least forty lines of mechanism the CLI cannot state.

nodes.label: Reference Verdict Zero
nodes.rationale: After tool-owned material moves to CLI surfaces, no remaining prose cluster is large enough to justify a separately loaded reference file.

nodes.label: Doctor-First Diagnosis
nodes.rationale: Doctor surfaces most known environmental failures faster than direct log inspection.

nodes.label: Result After Follow Redundancy

nodes.label: Armed Waiting
nodes.rationale: A managed run must have an armed watcher that wakes the caller when the run ends; merely starting it in the background leaves lifecycle work unfinished.

nodes.label: Measurement-Driven Refinement
nodes.rationale: Design claims are revised when live CLI, concurrency, or headless-session measurements disprove the plan.

nodes.label: Machine-Visible Help Audit Finish Line
nodes.rationale: One row per parser argument makes help coverage mechanically checkable, while semantic correctness remains a reading and adversarial-review task.

nodes.label: Fast Mode Discoverability
nodes.rationale: The priority tier was already implemented but undiscoverable because user-facing Codex calls it Fast mode while the bridge never used that name.

nodes.label: Help Claim Verification
nodes.rationale: New help wording is treated as an unverified claim until checked against Codex catalog/config evidence and exercised by a test that can fail.
